decisions.question: How should the native Windows failures caused by Unix-only tool-selection test paths be fixed?
decisions.choice: Create RU-021 as a narrow successor that depends on and supersedes RU-020 and directly supersedes the file-owning RU-017 for this test-only correction. Modify only the cfg(test) module in tool_selection_core so synthetic paths use a drive-rooted absolute path on Windows and slash-rooted absolute path elsewhere. Preserve production path validation and selection byte-for-byte. Rerun the unchanged current-product renderer gate, full locked native suite and unsigned private NSIS packaging workflow. Retain the accepted universal macOS artifact with its own exact source commit and hash.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within the product owner's explicit instruction to adapt and package Apple Silicon and Windows without incremental approval pauses

decisions.question: Which renderer tests should gate the current 野菜 Windows package after the jsdom repair proves inherited upstream App tests no longer describe this product?
decisions.choice: Create RU-020 as a narrow successor that depends on and supersedes RU-019. Retain its conditional matchMedia test polyfill, and change only the private manual Windows workflow so its renderer gate explicitly runs the current frozen candidate, diagnostics, configuration, service-catalog, billing and workbench test files while excluding release and inherited work trees. Keep cargo test --locked and the unsigned artifact-only NSIS path. Do not modify runtime source to satisfy obsolete upstream UI assertions.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within the product owner's explicit instruction to continue cross-platform packaging without incremental approval pauses

decisions.question: How should the clean-Windows matchMedia test-harness failure be corrected without reopening the accepted client or server architecture?
decisions.choice: Create RU-019 as a narrow successor that depends on and supersedes RU-018. Add a standards-shaped matchMedia polyfill only to tests/setupGlobals.ts, preserve every runtime and server file, rerun the existing manual private Windows artifact workflow, retain the already accepted notarized universal macOS DMG, and produce a replacement artifact receipt. Windows remains unsigned internal-test software with an expected SmartScreen warning; no public release or updater is created.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within the product owner's explicit instruction to continue cross-platform packaging without incremental approval pauses

decisions.question: How should the repaired client reach Apple Silicon and Windows internal testers, and what is the minimum future NewAPI persistence change?
decisions.choice: Create RU-018 as a packaging and handoff successor that depends on RU-017 without changing its runtime source. Build one signed and notarized universal macOS DMG with arm64 and x86_64 slices. Add a separate manual artifact-only Windows 2022 workflow for an unsigned NSIS internal installer in the private origin; do not use the inherited tag release workflow and do not publish a release or updater. For the server handoff, target deployed NewAPI v1.0.0-rc.27: reuse existing users, user_sessions, logs with Other JSON, tokens, pricing/options and top-up/payment records; keep pending device authorization codes in Redis with short TTL, one-time consumption and polling limits. Add no database schema by default. A later migration is allowed only if the server owner proves production schema drift or required immutable billing evidence cannot be retained in the existing JSON/options boundary. No server is changed in this unit.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within explicit cross-platform build and server-analysis request

decisions.question: How are these two installed-client defects repaired?
decisions.choice: Transparent native titlebar and fixed light/dark background retain native decorations. Do not force application or OS appearance, so system mode stays automatic. Version 2 deduplicates canonical aliases, excludes macOS .app internal executables before probing, selects only standalone candidate or unique earliest absolute PATH candidate. Ties and common-only ambiguity remain unresolved with desktop/retry actions. No user installation or configuration changes. Fixed five-tool closed projection includes independent and bundled counts and selection reason. Only selected candidate probed; never fall back silently after failure. Reject stale/malformed responses. v1 stays unchanged. Plain four-locale copy distinguishes Codex CLI. Test native selection, React/IPC theme ordering and scan transitions, workbench/cost regression and exact signed notarized local Intel package. No account, DSH, server, updater or public release activation. Keep 0.1.0; dated repair filename and hashes distinguish build, prior installer retained.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within explicit user repair request

decisions.question: May the verified renderer be built into a local installable artifact without claiming unfinished DSH and account features are complete?
decisions.choice: Build the current verified client as an Intel macOS local internal-test artifact using the existing candidate configuration and available Developer ID identity. Preserve version 0.1.0 and distinguish this build by dated filename and hashes. No runtime capability changes, server changes, GitHub publication, updater activation or claim of full-product readiness. The user has requested a version; creating an inspectable local artifact is an implementation step, not acceptance of a reduced final product. DSH launch/configuration and authenticated billing remain explicitly uncompleted.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within the user's request to build an installable client

decisions.question: Which independently deliverable client work may proceed while desktop account and historical billing endpoints are absent?
decisions.choice: Implement and verify the client cost-comparison presentation and an internal normalized receipt verifier as RU-015, superseding RU-014 renderer ownership only where required. Real account and billing data remain unavailable. No live producer, import route, mock runtime data, second numeric price table or billing-expression engine is added. The verifier checks signed-in subject/context, freshness, priced line arithmetic, currency conversion and same-cohort totals before any future authenticated producer may display an estimate. DSH runtime and packaging remain later independently verified work, not declared complete by this unit.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within product owner's client implementation request

decisions.question: May the initial DSH integration launch the official local interface in the user's browser instead of requiring a separate native or embedded window?
decisions.choice: Yes. The initial DSH experience uses the Yeschoy assistant as the launch entry and opens the official local web interface in the user's browser. Do not require a terminal step from beginners or embed the DSH interface into the privileged Yeschoy window. Version, installation, process lifecycle, configuration and credential verification remain prerequisites for a later implementation unit. This presentation decision does not approve all pricing proposals, change the existing release gate or authorize server changes.

decisions.question: What priorities and truth requirements does the owner add for DSH and usage-cost comparison?
decisions.choice: Prioritize investigation of DSH integration and require a visible, auditable comparison of official API cost for the same usage against actual Yeschoy charges. Record the research proposal without authorizing runtime behavior, server changes, an embedded DSH window, guessed billing data or a change to the existing DSH release gate. Preserve all historical frozen units.

decisions.question: How is the pnpm repository validated without changing product dependencies to satisfy an npm-only verification adapter?
decisions.choice: Supersede RU-012 with RU-013 solely to correct the test execution contract. Retain the accepted DEC-054 workbench scope and all no-server/no-secret/no-release boundaries. Use registered pytest-json scenarios to execute the unchanged selected React/Vitest tests via the locally locked Vitest installation, parse JSON reports, reject skipped or failed tests and use a temporary config/cache inside the verifier sandbox. No product scope, dependency, runtime command or source-isolation weakening is authorized.

decisions.question: Which visual correction replaces the rejected RU-011 presentation?
decisions.choice: Implement the approved compact blue/cyan workbench layout as RU-012, superseding RU-011 visual presentation only. Use a consistent system sans-serif type scale with monospace model IDs and tabular amounts, light/dark/system appearance stored only as a local preference, overview/app/model/billing navigation and cohesive configuration, diagnostics and settings. Preserve original app icon identity and all native contracts. Prototype values, mock authorization and mock connection completion must not enter runtime. Account, billing, recharge and configuration-write remain unavailable until separately implemented and verified. No server, release, signing or package distribution is authorized.

decisions.question: What product correction is authorized after the owner rejects the candidate icon, visual quality and command-line-first target model?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-011 as a client-only successor to RU-010. Make Claude Desktop and the graphical Codex surface the primary application targets; discover their actual desktop bundles separately from the preserved advanced CLI scanner. Replace the candidate landing presentation with a compact application-oriented desktop shell and original 野菜API leaf-and-route icon. The beginner path is application, line, real public model ID and connection readiness, with technical details secondary. Keep configuration application, secrets, login, balance, usage, recharge, installation, automatic update, telemetry, server and production changes blocked. Do not label detection, a documented provider interface or a public model declaration as proven end-to-end compatibility.

decisions.question: How should receipt completion consume evidence after the successor legitimately replaces files owned by its historical predecessor?
decisions.choice: Supersede RU-009 with RU-010 without changing product or packaging behavior. Keep the transitive frozen history and all prior reports. Replace the overlapping live predecessor-package prerequisite with a self-contained current-state run that executes all six RU-008 semantic scenarios and both RU-009 packaging checks under the same registered adapter and mandatory source isolation. Finish the signed-but-unnotarized local artifact receipt and explicit distribution limitations. Do not change global verifier code, skip tests, weaken signature checks, publish or modify servers.
decisions.decidedBy: product architecture within owner-authorized packaging continuation

decisions.question: How should the candidate packaging continue after discovering inherited URL registration and an unsuccessful first signing attempt?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-009 as a packaging-only successor to RU-008. Remove the inherited macOS URL registration at source, register no replacement protocol or login callback, and explicitly retain hardened runtime and disabled updater artifacts. Preserve all current runtime behavior and prior acceptance evidence. Rebuild from an identified clean source commit, verify the actual app and local DMG, and record signing, timestamp, architecture, contents, hashes, Gatekeeper and notarization separately. Only submit to Apple when user-configured local notarization credentials are available. No server, business credentials, application installation, runtime feature, public release or GitHub push changes.
decisions.decidedBy: product architecture within owner-authorized packaging continuation

decisions.question: How may the client reach a reproducible local signed candidate while preserving pnpm and failed governance history?
decisions.choice: Supersede RU-007 with RU-008 without changing product behavior. Replace the npm-only Vitest governance adapter with registered pytest-json@1 scenarios that execute real TypeScript contract/access modules and React components through an in-memory loader under mandatory read-only source isolation. Preserve the independent pnpm candidate tests and native suite, the old failed report, and all no-account/no-key/no-config-write boundaries. After tests pass, allow a macOS local candidate build signed by the installed Developer ID identity, with hardened runtime, no private-key export, no updater artifacts and no public distribution. Notarization is a separate Apple submission requiring user-configured local credentials and successful ticket verification. No NewAPI, server, CI, dependency-manager, global skill or product-feature changes.
decisions.decidedBy: product architecture within owner-authorized candidate packaging scope

decisions.question: What client-only integration may proceed while server changes belong to the owner's technical colleague?
decisions.choice: Supersede RU-005 with RU-007. Preserve prior local discovery, pure preview, account-unavailable, disabled apply/telemetry/updater and CI semantics; add a user-triggered native reader for anonymous GET /api/status, /api/pricing and /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap at the selected compiled first-party line only. Display actual public model IDs, group metadata, declared protocols and billing modes, with user-specific access explicitly unverified. Make tool/group/model selection produce a protocol-aware preview, not executable configuration. Reject stale, malformed, overlarge and redirected responses; do not parse group prose as protocol authority or use constant pricing_version as a cache revision. Deliver a machine-readable bootstrap handoff and complete prioritized backend integration checklist including the audited deployed revision, money-unit distinctions, session/key isolation and acceptance criteria. No server code, SSH, production changes, business login, key access, configuration read/write or paid model call in this unit.
decisions.decidedBy: product architecture under owner-authorized client-only scope

decisions.question: How should inherited upstream CI be adapted without expanding candidate runtime or release authority?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-006 as a CI-only unit depending on the completed RU-005 candidate. Replace main-only upstream checks with current candidate checks on main and product/** push and PR plus manual invocation; retain nightly scheduling by reusing the same workflow at the same commit. Run frontend type checking, current candidate tests and acceptance, Rust formatting/Clippy, and nonempty native test execution on Windows x64 and both macOS architectures. Keep native temp directories; fail for missing/current test identities, empty/ignored/filtered suites, compile and test failures. Do not compile the inactive CC Switch config module merely to preserve an irrelevant WSL write test. Explicitly state that this unit does not validate WSL configuration writes, signing, installers, runtime GUI, or production. No release, deployment, secret, repository-permission, NewAPI or product behavior change.

decisions.question: What is the official product display name?
decisions.choice: 野菜API

decisions.question: Who is V1 primarily for?
decisions.choice: Novice users who already installed an AI tool but cannot configure APIs, routes, models, or local files.

decisions.question: Which tools are in the V1 support set?
decisions.choice: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH (DeepSeek Harness).

decisions.question: Should V1 install third-party tools?
decisions.choice: No. V1 detects and configures existing installations; installation is deferred.

decisions.question: How transparent must model selection be?
decisions.choice: Show the exact model ID together with beginner-friendly labels, compatibility, and recommendations.

decisions.question: Does V1 compare pricing?
decisions.choice: Yes. Compare official vendor pricing with the authenticated user's actual 野菜API pricing using explicit input, output, cache, tier, and timestamp context.

decisions.question: What is the target account authorization experience?
decisions.choice: Open a first-party 野菜API website authorization page in the system browser; the website handles its existing login methods and grants the official client access.

decisions.question: May the current phase modify NewAPI or production infrastructure?
decisions.choice: No. Produce the client and a later backend-change specification only; do not change NewAPI, servers, Nginx, or production configuration now.

decisions.question: Should the client reuse CC Switch as a configuration-engine foundation?
decisions.choice: Proposed: fork or extract the Tauri/Rust configuration adapters, backup, and atomic-write mechanisms while replacing the product experience and adding first-party account/billing layers.

decisions.question: What measurable non-functional targets and verification environments must V1 meet?
decisions.choice: Pending product policy, platform support decisions, and measured baselines; do not invent numeric thresholds.

decisions.question: What are the official V1 line identities and root endpoints?
decisions.choice: Mainland optimized: https://yeschoy.com. Cloudflare global acceleration: https://api.yeschoy.com.

decisions.question: Do the two official lines have different account, key, model, or pricing semantics?
decisions.choice: No. They share account, API key, model availability, and pricing; only the network path differs.

decisions.question: Which models does the V1 model selector show by default, and what happens when a model is unavailable or removed?
decisions.choice: Default to models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; allow viewing all models with unavailable entries disabled and explained; never silently substitute a removed model.

decisions.question: Which source owns model availability, exact IDs, actual pricing, compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and official pricing?
decisions.choice: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, and actual user pricing. A versioned first-party 野菜API catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and sourced official pricing; it ships in the signed client until a future server interface distributes it.

decisions.question: What unit, currency, tier, and comparability rules govern official-versus-actual price display?
decisions.choice: Use CNY per one million tokens as the primary display, preserve official source currency, show a dated comparison-only exchange rate, separate input/output/cache and tier dimensions, preserve native units for non-token billing, and suppress savings claims when stale or incomparable.

decisions.question: Does the client automatically track short-term market exchange-rate movement for official-price comparison?
decisions.choice: No. V1 uses a fixed, versioned, comparison-only exchange rate and the product owner updates it only when movement is considered material; the exact value and change threshold remain unresolved.

decisions.question: What fixed USD-to-CNY rate does the initial signed model catalog use for price comparison?
decisions.choice: 1 USD = 6.75 CNY.

decisions.question: Which source owns the numeric official-price baseline and the current user's actual price?
decisions.choice: NewAPI owns both numeric values: its governed base pricing is the official-price baseline and its user, group, and special billing rules produce the actual price. The desktop client does not duplicate price numbers; its signed catalog only supplements compatibility, descriptions, recommendations, and price provenance metadata until NewAPI exposes that metadata.

decisions.question: What invariant distinguishes NewAPI official-price fields from 野菜API discounts?
decisions.choice: NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions always store the corresponding vendor official price. User discounts, promotions, and channel-specific adjustments are applied only through separately identifiable group ratios or special billing rules and never overwrite the official baseline.

decisions.question: How does the official desktop client complete first-party account authorization?
decisions.choice: Use a system-browser device authorization flow: request a short-lived single-use device code, let the website perform normal login and explicit device approval, poll for completion, then store a device-scoped session in the operating system credential store. No password, website cookie, API key, or final session credential appears in a URL. Cancellation, rejection, expiry, network interruption, logout, and website-side device revocation are explicit states.

decisions.question: What expiry, refresh, reauthorization, and revocation rules govern a desktop account session?
decisions.choice: The single-use device code expires after 10 minutes. The access token expires after one hour and refreshes automatically. The remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and requires reauthorization after an absolute maximum of 90 days. Logout or website-side device revocation removes refresh eligibility; the next online request clears local account credentials and enters an explicit revoked state. A long-offline client that cannot refresh requires login again, and sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

decisions.question: At what granularity are relay API keys created and reused?
decisions.choice: Create one independent relay API key per account, device, and supported tool. Reuse it idempotently across repeated configuration, line changes, and model changes. A different device gets different keys. If a reinstall cannot prove the prior device identity, treat it as a new device and leave old keys active until explicit revocation.

decisions.question: How do logout, device revocation, local configuration removal, and individual tool-key rotation differ?
decisions.choice: Logout clears only the desktop account session. Revoking a lost or untrusted device also revokes every tool key for that device. Individual tool-key rotation creates the replacement, backs up and writes the target configuration, verifies it, and only then revokes the old key; failure preserves the old key and restores the original configuration. Removing local tool configuration asks separately whether its remote key should also be revoked.

decisions.question: Does V1 retain configuration backup history, and what rollback artifact may exist during a write?
decisions.choice: V1 retains no configuration backup history. A material write may create only an encrypted temporary rollback snapshot for the active transaction. Successful validation deletes it immediately; failure restores from it and deletes it after recovery. A crash may leave only an unfinished-transaction snapshot for recovery on the next launch. The snapshot is never uploaded or used for cross-device restore, and a secure-storage failure blocks the write rather than falling back to plaintext.

decisions.question: Should the client reuse CC Switch as a configuration-engine foundation after persistent backup history is excluded?
decisions.choice: Directly fork the CC Switch Tauri/Rust/Web project as the technical foundation. Reuse only reviewed configuration adapters, atomic-write, process/path detection, and release engineering; replace the provider-centric experience with 野菜API branding, first-party account and billing, novice guidance, diagnostics, and telemetry. Preserve MIT notices, audit dependency licenses, use only ephemeral encrypted rollback snapshots, and review rather than automatically merge upstream changes.

decisions.question: Which account and key-management capabilities may a desktop device session exercise?
decisions.choice: Apply least privilege. The session may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices; create or reuse, rotate, and revoke only the current device's per-tool relay keys; and log out the current device. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings are website-only or inaccessible to the desktop session.

decisions.question: Which Windows and macOS versions and CPU architectures are officially supported in V1?
decisions.choice: Officially support Windows 10 22H2 x64 and Windows 11 x64, with a visible Windows 10 end-of-support warning. Treat Windows 11 ARM64 running the x64 build under emulation as best-effort, not officially supported. Officially support macOS 13 and later and ship a Universal binary for Intel and Apple Silicon. Install or guide installation of the official WebView2 runtime when absent.

decisions.question: How is macOS V1 distributed while minimizing prominent exposure of the individual signer identity?
decisions.choice: Distribute a signed and notarized Universal DMG from the first-party 野菜API website and do not list V1 in the Mac App Store. Use the existing individual Apple Developer Program membership and Developer ID. Product pages and ordinary UI do not proactively display the personal legal name, while the product makes no anonymity promise and accepts that technical certificate inspection can identify the signer.

decisions.question: How does public release proceed while Windows lacks a signing identity?
decisions.choice: Continue Windows and macOS development and testing in parallel, allow the signed and notarized macOS build to publish first, and keep Windows internal until trusted signing is available. Prefer a 野菜API organization publisher, but accept a personal publisher identity as the fallback. Never publish an unsigned or self-signed Windows package to novice users; select direct signing or Store MSIX only after release-engineering validation.

decisions.question: Is operational telemetry uploaded by default, and what privacy boundary governs it?
decisions.choice: Use first-party basic operational telemetry enabled by default to detect failures early. Before any upload, provide conspicuous plain-language notice and an easy disable control that does not affect core functionality. Enforce a strict allowlist for versions, platform, tool and adapter identity, operation stage/result/error/duration, line class, model ID, sanitized crash fingerprint and stack, and a rotating pseudonymous telemetry ID separated from account and device authorization identity. Never automatically upload secrets, prompts, responses, project content, complete paths, OS usernames, clipboard content, full configuration, or raw memory dumps.

decisions.question: How long are telemetry events, crash envelopes, aggregate trends, identifiers, and pending local uploads retained?
decisions.choice: Retain ordinary operational events for 30 days, sanitized crash events and code stacks for 90 days, and irreversibly de-identified aggregate trends for 12 months. Rotate the pseudonymous telemetry ID every 30 days and expire the local pending-upload queue after seven days. Disabling telemetry immediately clears the local queue and may request deletion of raw historical events; incident-specific retention extensions require a recorded scope, reason, approver, and deletion date.

decisions.question: What stable application identifier does the desktop product use across packaging, credential storage, and updates?
decisions.choice: Use com.yeschoy.desktop as the official stable application identifier.

decisions.question: Should the official desktop client directly consume NewAPI's broad website session and generic token CRUD interfaces?
decisions.choice: Proposed: add a versioned, least-privilege desktop API boundary that reuses NewAPI domain services internally but exposes only device authorization, current-account read projections, and current-device per-tool key operations. Do not treat the proposed /api/desktop/v1 paths as existing until implemented and verified against the deployed instance.

decisions.question: Where should complex official-versus-actual pricing semantics be evaluated for the desktop client?
decisions.choice: Proposed: NewAPI produces a versioned desktop pricing projection and quote result from its canonical base pricing, group ratios, and special billing expressions. The desktop displays the projection and never implements a second billing-expression interpreter or numeric price table.

decisions.question: May the fork retain the upstream update identity or use ordinary local storage for 野菜API account and tool secrets?
decisions.choice: Proposed: no. Replace or disable every CC Switch update endpoint and key before release, establish an independent 野菜API update trust root, and keep desktop sessions, tool keys, and rollback keys only in an explicit operating-system credential vault rather than ordinary SQLite, logs, or front-end persistence.

decisions.question: How should Claude Code and Codex receive their per-tool relay keys without leaving plaintext secrets in their normal configuration files?
decisions.choice: Keep each key only in the operating-system credential vault and ship a signed local credential helper. Configure Claude Code through apiKeyHelper and Codex through model_providers.yeschoy.auth.command. Do not write ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, experimental_bearer_token, or a 野菜 key in auth.json. A tool version that cannot use the verified helper contract is unsupported for one-click configuration rather than receiving a plaintext fallback.

decisions.question: How should OpenCode, Pi, and DSH receive their per-tool relay keys while preserving the confirmed operating-system-vault and no-plaintext-fallback boundary?
decisions.choice: OpenCode loads a signed 野菜 auth plugin whose runtime loader calls the credential helper; Pi uses its native models.json apiKey !command contract; DSH installs a pinned out-of-tree credential provider that resolves the 野菜 credential reference from the operating-system vault instead of .credentials.yaml. Each integration is version-gated and fail-closed, and no tool receives a plaintext fallback.

decisions.question: Which DSH profiles may 野菜API V1 configure automatically?
decisions.choice: V1 configures only the DSH web profile. Headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp, and any other profile are read-only discovery targets that show an unsupported-for-automatic-configuration status and receive no plugin, patch, settings, or credential writes.

decisions.question: How should 野菜API V1 decide whether an installed third-party tool version is safe to configure automatically?
decisions.choice: Use a signed exact-version allowlist produced only by the complete Windows and macOS adapter matrix. At each release baseline, test the latest three stable versions of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi; evaluate DSH separately against one exact prerelease tag. Do not infer support from a minimum version or open semver range. Unknown, newly released, failed, or prerelease versions outside the explicit DSH evaluation remain read-only until a signed client update adds verified evidence.

decisions.question: How should DSH be presented in V1 given that its current upstream tag is prerelease but the product owner considers the version materially settled?
decisions.choice: Treat an exact allowlisted DSH web version as a normal V1 supported tool without a Developer Preview product badge. Continue to display the exact upstream version in advanced details and diagnostics, and do not claim support until that exact tag passes the same mandatory platform, credential, configuration, request, recovery, removal, and secret-leak gates. This product presentation decision does not rename the upstream tag or infer compatibility for another DSH tag or profile.

decisions.question: Must a fully verified normal-support DSH web adapter be complete before the agreed V1 product may be released?
decisions.choice: No. DSH web remains a normal V1 support target, but its incomplete compatibility does not block the overall V1 release. If no exact DSH version has passed the mandatory matrix at release time, the client reports DSH as detected but not currently supported for automatic configuration, performs no configuration or credential writes, and may add normal support later only through a trusted signed client update after the exact version passes.

decisions.question: What is the first implementation release unit authorized for the 野菜API desktop client?
decisions.choice: Freeze and implement RU-001 only: establish the 野菜API desktop shell and brand, then perform local read-only discovery and truthful compatibility reporting for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH. The unit performs no network request, account or billing action, NewAPI change, credential access, configuration read or write, third-party installation, automatic update, or telemetry upload. Until a later signed exact-version allowlist is verified, every detected version remains read-only and is never presented as ready for one-click configuration.

decisions.question: What client-only successor release unit is authorized after RU-001 when the deployed NewAPI still lacks the approved desktop authorization boundary?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-002 as a successor to RU-001. Preserve the branded five-tool read-only discovery experience and add the production account and billing information architecture, complete page states, fixed display-only 1 USD = 6.75 CNY context, and an updated future NewAPI change specification. The only runtime account projection in this unit is backend_upgrade_required: it performs no account network request, stores no credential, shows no fabricated account or numeric billing value, and exposes no active recharge or authorization action until a later frozen unit verifies a deployed least-privilege /api/desktop/v1 contract.

decisions.question: Which future server boundary may activate the desktop account and billing shell?
decisions.choice: Only a versioned first-party /api/desktop/v1 boundary may activate it. The future server reuses NewAPI domain services internally but exposes device authorization, device-scoped rotating sessions, narrow current-account and usage projections, server-evaluated official-versus-actual pricing, and a first-party wallet URL. The desktop must not use broad website cookies, browser access tokens, generic token CRUD, or a client-side billing-expression interpreter as a shortcut.

decisions.question: What implementation boundary should follow RU-002 before the real desktop backend, model catalog, credential helpers, and exact-version allowlist are available?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-003 as a client-only successor to RU-002. Add a complete beginner configuration-preview flow for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH with the approved mainland and global line roots, evidenced per-tool target fields, and deterministic protocol-endpoint derivation. Keep model ID explicitly unavailable and keep apply, connectivity testing, credential access, configuration reads and writes, rollback, server calls, and production changes blocked. DSH shows the selected line root but no derived protocol endpoint or write target until an exact web-profile adapter is verified.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: What bounded implementation unit may finish the client-side V1 candidate after RU-004 without implying that backend-dependent or release-security capabilities are ready?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-005 as a client-side V1 candidate successor that supersedes RU-004. Preserve the account, billing, five-tool discovery, and configuration-preview truth boundaries; add one beginner home journey, a user-triggered read-only diagnostic that resolves and attempts TCP port 443 only for yeschoy.com and api.yeschoy.com without credentials or API payloads, and a settings and security surface that exposes language, privacy, secret, backup, update, and release state. Prepare but do not publish Windows and macOS candidate bundles, keep updater artifacts and telemetry upload disabled, label Windows unsigned beta limitations and macOS signing and notarization as unmet release gates, and update the future NewAPI handoff without modifying any server or production resource.

decisions.question: How should the desktop workbench communicate with nontechnical users?
decisions.choice: Keep the existing installable Tauri desktop architecture and approved look.
